body:
#### Triton operator validation (v0.32.0 · A3 / A5)

Tested PR head `965da18e0a4adcadf37b5a32a2f56a1250970ca6` with vLLM **v0.32.0** (`5df63a7203cdb9328d824a27b682e77c7b9928be`), Torch `2.10.0+cpu`, TorchNPU `2.10.0.post7`, Triton Ascend `3.6.0.post2`, and Transformers `5.19.0`.

1. **Functionality:** GLM KDA accepted-state commit and aligned boundary snapshots passed on A3 `Ascend910_9382` and A5 `Ascend950DT_9581`. Each device passed **212 tests**, including eager/NPU graph execution, H32/H64, K=V=128, Q1/Q2/Q4/Q6/Q8, FP32/BF16 checkpoints, strided metadata, mixed boundary requests and in-place/out-of-place writes. The operator documentation and tests are included in this PR.
2. **Accuracy:** Each device passed **1,552 operator-output comparisons against independent FP64 references**, excluding accuracy-checker control tests. Every output achieved a **100% mixed-tolerance pass rate** and met its maximum-error cap; copy-only outputs and untouched regions matched exactly. Maximum errors across both devices: BF16 `0.003865179`, FP16 `2.28976e-05`, FP32 `4.112112e-07`. Full-model GSM8K results with ReplaySSM OFF → ON: **A3 1278 → 1277/1319 (-0.076 pp); A5 1280 → 1277/1319 (-0.227 pp)**. These observed score changes and paired errors are retained; one paired run does **not** establish numerical equivalence or non-inferiority.
3. **Performance:** The same-runtime operator A/B sweep compares PR base `981f02b55244982d66ae9237e2a6062e211ff1ef` with this head, using 60 cases/device and seven alternating NPU-graph timing rounds. The separate whole-model comparison uses **the same PR source**, changing only `--no-use-replayssm` / `--use-replayssm`, with prefix caching and target/MTP graphs enabled in both arms. C90 results below use official vLLM SSE ITL in a verified all-worker D90/P0 window; they are not TPOT and are not divided by tokens per SSE event. Gains and regressions are both reported below.
4. **Safety:** The 37 `tl.constexpr` annotations are unchanged; `num_layers` is a runtime argument with `do_not_specialize`. UB budgeting uses the actual FP32 correction tensor element size and the grouped two-head factor. Changing accepted lengths and boundary membership after warmup added zero JIT entries in the operator sweep. Dataset compiler entries, JIT memory-cache changes and persistent artifacts are reported below, scoped to the audited Triton kernels. Native OFF has no independent RecoverSSM commit kernel; this does not mean native KDA has zero cost.

<details>
<summary>Whole-model configuration, accuracy, acceptance and SSE latency</summary>

Both arms use prefix caching, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, draft `enforce_eager=false`, MTP5, BF16 model activations/KV, FP32 SSM state, PP/PCP/DCP=1, seed 1024, and disabled async scheduling. A3 uses W8A8 weights, DP8/TP2/EP16, batched-token budget 4096 and memory utilization 0.90; A5 uses MXFP8 weights, DP8/TP1/EP8, budget 256 and memory utilization 0.94. Model length is 16384, with 12 maximum requests per DP rank. CPU binding/shared-expert DP are enabled; fused MC2/shared-expert multistream overlap are disabled.

The same fixed shared-prefix messages and 90 question suffixes are used throughout; workload SHA256 `1b42b6e1ed541f0398521f4599dd079f5b4bbd25bfe2cd275f139040f2e6e9f7`. Real DP request counts are `12/12/11/11/11/11/11/11`. Each arm has a 90×64-token warmup, three unprofiled timing batches (natural EOS, max_tokens=3072, no min_tokens), and independent profiling requests. Each table entry for ITL is the median of the three batch statistics. Acceptance counters are whole-batch Prometheus deltas, separate from the common D90/P0 ITL window.

| Device | OFF Mean SSE ITL (ms) | ON Mean SSE ITL (ms) | Change | C90 draft acceptance OFF → ON | C90 length incl. bonus OFF → ON |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 | 73.339 | 69.891 | -4.70% | 24.733% → 24.859% | 2.237 → 2.243 |
| A5 | 44.801 | 44.078 | -1.62% | 24.929% → 25.156% | 2.246 → 2.258 |

GSM8K uses all 1319 questions, the same shared prefix, 90 HTTP workers, temperature 0, seed 1024, max_tokens=8192 and no output retries. The primary grader normalizes thousands commas/spaces; original answers, token IDs and legacy scores are retained.

| Device | OFF canonical accuracy | ON canonical accuracy | Change | Newly wrong | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 | 1278/1319 (96.892%) | 1277/1319 (96.816%) | -0.076 pp | 8 | 7 |
| A5 | 1280/1319 (97.043%) | 1277/1319 (96.816%) | -0.227 pp | 11 | 8 |

The flag changes the default derived cache-page geometry. Every request is checked for real complete-block shared-prefix hits; the input messages and serving arguments are otherwise unchanged. TTFT therefore includes different amounts of remaining prefill and must not be presented as a pure decode gain.

| Device | OFF block tokens | ON block tokens | Required OFF cached tokens/request | Required ON cached tokens/request |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 | 2304 | 2432 | 4608 | 4864 |
| A5 | 4480 | 4864 | 4480 | 4864 |

| Device | Full-batch TTFT mean (ms), OFF → ON | Steady received output tokens/s, OFF → ON | Full GSM8K acceptance, OFF → ON | GSM8K length incl. bonus, OFF → ON |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 | 2351.871 → 2089.080 | 2703.846 → 2840.994 | 63.157% → 63.453% | 4.158 → 4.173 |
| A5 | 2806.569 → 1612.028 | 4429.879 → 4517.828 | 63.765% → 63.955% | 4.188 → 4.198 |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Same-runtime operator A/B performance and layout provenance</summary>

The microbenchmark retains the model cache-field shapes, physical strides and full pool capacity. Cache geometry comes from this runtime's original JIT observations, including smaller eager/dataset batches; B11/B12 come from independently verified C90 worker counts, and L11/L12 from the commit contexts. Native graph replay does not re-enter Python, so a Python B12 JIT launch is not claimed. FP32 checkpoint/correction and BF16 key/gate records share the same page allocation. Each case uses seven alternating A/B rounds with 32 native graph replays and NPU-event timing; no profiler is active.

The table shows B12/L12/accepted3, in ms. State time includes state kernels only; context time includes plan, convolution and state. This is a different baseline from the full-model native OFF / ReplaySSM ON comparison.

| Device | Case | Base state (ms) | Candidate state (ms) | State change | Full context base → candidate (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 | no_cross | 1.310 | 0.854 | -34.81% | 1.349 → 0.871 |
| A3 | mixed | 1.338 | 1.095 | -18.16% | 1.383 → 1.125 |
| A3 | cross | 1.345 | 1.364 | +1.45% | 1.396 → 1.413 |
| A3 | exact | 1.410 | 1.437 | +1.96% | 1.456 → 1.482 |
| A3 | unaligned | 0.850 | 0.836 | -1.67% | 0.853 → 0.854 |
| A5 | no_cross | 1.673 | 0.564 | -66.27% | 1.699 → 0.593 |
| A5 | mixed | 1.787 | 0.999 | -44.09% | 1.821 → 1.033 |
| A5 | cross | 1.807 | 1.454 | -19.51% | 1.846 → 1.495 |
| A5 | exact | 1.846 | 1.588 | -13.95% | 1.881 → 1.624 |
| A5 | unaligned | 0.524 | 0.525 | +0.16% | 0.551 → 0.552 |

A3 full state-latency ranges: cross: -0.56% to +2.64%; exact: -0.74% to +2.44%; mixed: -29.66% to -11.50%; no_cross: -54.10% to -20.53%; unaligned: -3.00% to +2.46%. Maximum A/B state difference `0`; the independent FP64 tests above provide the separate mathematical reference.

A5 full state-latency ranges: cross: -20.66% to -13.67%; exact: -14.85% to -12.27%; mixed: -47.38% to -36.33%; no_cross: -69.73% to -55.23%; unaligned: -0.32% to +0.75%. Maximum A/B state difference `3.72529e-09`; the independent FP64 tests above provide the separate mathematical reference.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Independent CPU/NPU profiling and full-dataset compilation audit</summary>

Each worker contributes ten complete D90/P0 forwards. All 48 raw traces are checked against original CPU native graph-replay scopes, per-worker forward records, CANN MODEL_EXECUTE records and NPU tasks. CPU scopes and NPU tasks are checked independently; no complete per-kernel ACL-to-NPU flow linkage is claimed. State-commit values are NPU kernel sums per worker forward, not ITL or a critical-path measurement.

| Device | ReplaySSM | Raw traces | Target replay scopes | Draft prefill scopes | Draft decode scopes | CANN MODEL_EXECUTE records | Commit NPU sum/worker forward (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 | OFF | 16 | 160 | 160 | 160 | 480 | N/A: native path |
| A3 | ON | 16 | 160 | 160 | 160 | 480 | 2.061 |
| A5 | OFF | 8 | 80 | 80 | 80 | 240 | N/A: native path |
| A5 | ON | 8 | 80 | 80 | 80 | 240 | 1.532 |

| Device | ReplaySSM | Dataset compiler-entry events | JIT memory-cache changes | New persistent files | Modified persistent files | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A3 | OFF | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Native path; RecoverSSM kernels not called |
| A3 | ON | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Audited RecoverSSM kernels |
| A5 | OFF | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Native path; RecoverSSM kernels not called |
| A5 | ON | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Audited RecoverSSM kernels |

Every new Python JIT-launch metadata signature and memory-cache change is retained, and compiler-entry hooks remain active on every entry. Startup/warmup and dataset phases are distinguished; graph replay is independently proven by CPU/NPU evidence. Compiled identifiers and all raw rounds, JUnit metrics, SSE/IDs, CANN traces, source hashes and measurement scripts are retained in the validation bundle.

A5 OFF trial0 was recovered from its complete raw 90-request recording after correcting an inherited 4864-token cache-hit assumption: this release's native path resolves 4480-token blocks. All saved ITL/TTFT, SSE/IDs and worker graph-window checks were revalidated, without rerunning that valid trial. Its unsaved Python batch wall-clock boundaries remain null; steady ITL and received-output metrics use the preserved original timestamps.

</details>
